qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Massive proprietary R&D scale, global veterinary direct sales distribution network, deep patent estates for novel biologics (monoclonal antibodies like Librela/Solensia, JAK inhibitors like Apoquel/Cytopoint), and entrenched veterinary trust prevent competitive arbitrage. Empirical proof: sustained 30%+ GAAP ROIC (median 30.5%), ~70% gross margins, and consistent 2-4% annual price realization. Primary erosion threats: adverse event regulatory warnings and pet owner caution on novel biologics, emerging competition from Elanco/Boehringer Ingelheim, and generic erosion in mature livestock anti-infectives.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Global leader in animal health medicines and vaccines. Moat anchored by deep veterinary distribution, high-margin proprietary biologics, and cash-pay pet economics insulated from government reimbursement cliffs. Strong cash conversion (82.5% FCF conversion) and comfortable balance sheet (3.38x debt/NI, 16.1x interest coverage). [5-10Y g: companion animal volume 3.5% + veterinary pricing power 2.5% + international expansion 1.5% - adverse event / regulatory conservatism drag 0.5% + net share buybacks 1.5%]
qualitative.evidence: 10-year GAAP ROIC consistently between 19.4% and 31.6% (5-year median 30.5%), with operating tangible ROIC exceeding 54%. Multi-year Owner FCF conversion of 82.5% (FY2025 Owner FCF of $2,334M on $2,673M Net Income). Revenue grew from $4,888M in FY2016 to $9,467M in FY2025 with operating income rising from $1,394M to $3,582M. Unbroken peak-to-peak Owner EPS compounding ($1.70 in 2016 to $6.02 in 2025, CAGR 12.0%). Long-term debt of $9,042M against $2,312M cash (net debt $6,730M) yields net debt / NI of 2.52x and interest coverage of 16.1x, providing durable balance sheet resilience through industry cycles.
